title: Sum a periodic sequence using complete repeating blocks
content: If a sequence defined by a recurrence relation turns out to be periodic (it repeats every k terms), you can find the sum of many terms without a standard AP/GP formula. Work out how many complete blocks of k terms fit into the total number of terms required, multiply the sum of one block by that number of complete blocks, then add on the sum of any leftover terms at the end. For example, with a period-2 sequence and 85 terms, there are 42 complete pairs (84 terms) plus 1 leftover term.
